observations: Short visible trunk, with internal fine branching beneath an almost continuous foliage dome.
Crown is broad with uneven peripheral tufts; lower-left negative spaces and smaller exposed limbs, not an open cork-oak fork.
Foliage is deep muted olive with gray-green surfaces and dark interiors; bark is finely scaled rather than thick cork.
analysis.hypothesis: Branch-supported sprays along multiple branch intervals and broader overlapping crown sectors can reproduce the dense evergreen mass without spherical meshes.

iterationHistory.reason: Actual render too upright, discrete lobes and yellow-green palette.

iterationHistory.candidate: Broader connected branch envelope with texture albedo retained
iterationHistory.reason: Broad connected silhouette and muted foliage closer to supplied reference; edge lobes and internal highlight shapes still too repetitive.

review.reviewer: Primary Codex via actual supplied images and captured beauty, silhouette, branch and scene images; no independent review

remaining.defect: Repeated crown scallops and clump boundaries
remaining.evidence: The silhouette still resolves into similar-sized peripheral lobes, unlike the photograph’s finer, more irregular connected outline.
Large green highlight patches and simplified interior shading lack the photo’s subtle gray-green leaf variation; bark detail is strongest only at close view.
The trunk and root flare are comparatively regular; real reference has more individual character and asymmetric fine branching.
